Alex Chen: Quick sync — Large enterprise prospect asked for: full audit export (raw events), per-tenant BYOK key support, SOC2/ISO evidence package, and 7+ year retention options. They want a pilot by end of Q3. Thoughts on minimum viable scope?
Mari Patel: Thanks. We need launch acceptance criteria and a pricing approach (add-on vs included). Also confirm what counts as the 'evidence package'.
Jordan K.: From runtime side: raw event export + per-tenant KMS is doable but nontrivial. BYOK handshake + rotation + escrow adds ~3-4 sprints if we do HSM integration and proof-of-possession flows.
Liz H.: Evidence package = filtered audit bundle (auth events, admin actions, config snapshots, model version metadata) + tamper-evident hashes and access logs for retrieval. SOC2 auditor will expect chain-of-custody docs.
Pat Gomez: Customer says they'll sign a 1yr commitment if we support per-tenant BYOK and a 3 year retention SLA. They're willing to pay a premium.
Alex Chen: Ok — proposal: pilot MVP = (1) raw audit export endpoint + streaming S3 export (2) retention tiers 90d / 1yr / 3yr (cold archive) (3) BYOK for export-at-rest only (no full HSM rotation) (4) baseline evidence package for SOC2. Does that feel acceptable?
Mari Patel: That MVP reduces scope. We should define exact acceptance tests: sample export for 10k events, proof-of-key-ownership docs, retrieval time for cold archive <= 24h. Add: legal hold toggle.
Jordan K.: Technical constraints: cold archive will be object storage w/ lifecycle policies. Retrieval SLA 24h is fine. For BYOK-at-rest we can support envelope encryption with customer KEK; full HSM signing sequence is later. Work estimate: 6 weeks to get envelope BYOK and export pipeline stable.
Liz H.: Need to add: key-revocation playbook and on-demand evidence freeze. Auditors want immutable snapshots with notarized timestamps if possible.
Pat Gomez: Pricing note: customers expect audit exports as an enterprise add-on. We should present two commercial options: (A) retention as a metered storage add-on + BYOK flat fee, (B) an all-in enterprise bundle with committed monthly fee and discounted storage. Which do we prefer?
Alex Chen: Let's map both to product requirements. Option A easier to ship fast. Option B higher ARR but more implementation nuance.
Mari Patel: Can we outline what to ship in sprint 1 vs sprint 2? I propose sprint 1 (pilot): export endpoint, envelope BYOK for S3 exports, 90d & 1yr retention. Sprint 2: cold archive 3yr, legal-hold APIs, evidence notarization, key-rotation flows.
Jordan K.: Agreed. Also include a conformance test harness: a script that replays N events through the export and verifies presence/hash. I'll draft a small test harness.
Alex Chen: Add a short sample config snippet for the export API we can share with sales.
Alex Chen: ```json
{
  "export": {
    "target": "s3://customer-bucket/...",
    "encryption": "customer-kek",
    "retention": "1yr",
    "format": "ndjson",
    "legal_hold": false
  }
}
```
Mari Patel: Nice. Jordan — can you attach rough dev estimates to each sprint item by EOD? We need to present to GTM on Monday.
Jordan K.: Will do. Quick estimates now: sprint 1 ~6w (2 engs), sprint 2 ~8w (3 engs) including security review and infra work.
Liz H.: I'll draft the auditor checklist and the key revocation/runbook. Also: we must include KMS access logging (customer KMS + our control plane) as part of evidence.
Pat Gomez: For customer conversations, I'll map the two commercial options to example pricing math: storage @ $0.02/GB-mo, BYOK onboarding $15k one-time, bundle starting $50k/mo for mid-sized customer. These are placeholders.
Alex Chen: Good. Risks: legal escrow for keys, cross-region export latency, regulatory data residency. Call these out in the roadmap.
Mari Patel: Action items: Jordan — dev estimates + test harness. Liz — auditor checklist + runbook. Pat — draft commercial options and appetite indicator. Alex — compile launch acceptance criteria doc. All by Friday.
sre-bot: Reminder set — follow-up sync scheduled Friday 10am PT. :calendar:
